decks.name: Anatomy II: Cortex, Deep Nuclei & Cerebellum (Board Review)

zeilen: Pyramidal cells → commissural and association fibers
Main **thalamic sensory input**; enlarged in sensory cortex; band of Baillarger (stria of Gennari in V1)
**Betz cells** → brainstem/spinal cord; enlarged in motor cortex
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 31–32. Archicortex (hippocampus, dentate) has 3 layers.

zeilen: Frontal eye field (saccades to the contralateral side)

cards.vorderseite: Frontal eye field: function and lesion
cards.rueckseite: Area 8 (caudal middle frontal gyrus). Initiates **voluntary saccades to the contralateral side** (via PPRF/riMLF, not directly to CN nuclei). Irritative lesion (seizure) → eyes deviate **away** from the lesion; destructive lesion → eyes deviate **toward** the lesion.

SMA = medial area 6, anterior to the leg motor area. Resection → transient contralateral **akinesia/hemiparesis** and (dominant side) **reduced spontaneous speech**, which typically **recovers within weeks**.

Right-handers: almost always **left** dominant. Left-handers: ~**85% left**, ~15% bilateral, rarely right.
Dominant angular/supramarginal lesion → **Gerstmann syndrome** (agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia, left–right confusion). Nondominant inferior parietal lesion → **neglect**, anosognosia.

cards.vorderseite: Surface landmarks: pterion, sylvian fissure, motor strip
cards.rueckseite:
**Pterion:** ~3 cm behind the frontozygomatic point along the sylvian line (H-shaped suture junction).
**Sylvian fissure:** line from frontozygomatic point to the 75% point of the nasion–inion line.
**Rolandic (central) sulcus:** upper end ~2 cm behind the midpoint of nasion–inion; **motor strip ~4–5 cm behind the coronal suture**.

- **Anterior:** mammillothalamic tract → cingulate (Papez)
- **VA / VL:** basal ganglia and cerebellum (dentate) → motor/premotor cortex; **VIM** = tremor target
- **VPL:** medial lemniscus + spinothalamic (body) → S1
- **VPM:** trigeminal (face) + taste (VPMpc) → S1/area 43
- **LGB:** vision → V1; **MGB:** hearing (inferior colliculus) → Heschl
- **Mediodorsal:** limbic/prefrontal; lesion → Korsakoff
- **Pulvinar:** visual association
- **Reticular nucleus:** GABAergic gate, no cortical projection

6 layers: **crossed** fibers (contralateral eye) → layers **1, 4, 6**; **uncrossed** (ipsilateral) → **2, 3, 5**. Layers 1–2 magnocellular, 3–6 parvocellular. No binocular fusion at this level.
Lower retina → lateral LGB → lower bank of calcarine (Meyer loop, temporal lobe).

- **Anterior limb:** anterior thalamic radiation, frontopontine fibers
- **Genu:** **corticobulbar** fibers
- **Posterior limb:** **corticospinal** (arm anterior → leg posterior), superior thalamic radiation (sensory behind motor)
- **Retrolenticular:** optic radiation
- **Sublenticular:** auditory radiation

cards.vorderseite: Pineal gland: function and light pathway
cards.rueckseite: Secretes **melatonin** (max in darkness). Light → retina → **suprachiasmatic nucleus** → hypothalamus → intermediolateral column (upper thoracic) → **superior cervical ganglion** → sympathetic fibers inhibit the pineal. Pineal destruction (tumor) in boys → **precocious puberty**.

cards.vorderseite: Basal ganglia: direct and indirect pathways
cards.rueckseite:
**Direct:** cortex → striatum (D1, GABA/substance P) ⊣ **GPi/SNr** ⊣ thalamus (VA/VL) → cortex: **facilitates** movement.
**Indirect:** striatum (D2, GABA/enkephalin) ⊣ GPe ⊣ **STN** → (glutamate) GPi/SNr ⊣ thalamus: **inhibits** movement.
Dopamine (SNc) excites direct (D1) and inhibits indirect (D2). Parkinson: overactive STN/GPi → targets for DBS.

cards.vorderseite: Pallidal outflow: ansa lenticularis vs. lenticular fasciculus
cards.rueckseite:
**Ansa lenticularis:** from GPi, loops **around** the internal capsule ("ansa goes around") → Forel field H.
**Lenticular fasciculus (H2):** from GPi **through** the internal capsule, ventral to zona incerta.
Both join with the **cerebellothalamic** fibers as the **thalamic fasciculus (H1)** → VA/VL.

cards.vorderseite: Substantia nigra: pars compacta vs. pars reticulata
cards.rueckseite:
**Pars compacta:** dorsal, **dopaminergic** (neuromelanin) → striatum; degenerates in Parkinson disease.
**Pars reticulata:** ventral (near crus cerebri), **GABAergic**; output → VA/MD thalamus, **superior colliculus** (saccades), pedunculopontine nucleus; functionally equivalent to GPi.

- **Supraoptic/paraventricular:** ADH, oxytocin → posterior pituitary
- **Suprachiasmatic:** circadian clock
- **Anterior:** heat loss (lesion → hyperthermia), parasympathetic
- **Posterior:** heat conservation (lesion → poikilothermia), sympathetic, arousal
- **Ventromedial:** satiety (lesion → obesity)
- **Lateral:** feeding (lesion → starvation)
- **Arcuate:** releasing hormones, dopamine → portal system

**Adenohypophysis:** oral ectoderm (**Rathke pouch**, stomodeum roof). **Neurohypophysis:** diencephalic neuroectoderm.
Portal system: **superior hypophyseal arteries** (supraclinoid ICA) → median eminence/infundibulum capillaries → portal veins → anterior lobe. **Inferior hypophyseal artery** (meningohypophyseal trunk) → posterior lobe.

The **only sensory system without an obligatory thalamic relay** to its primary cortex. Receptors (bipolar) → through **cribriform plate** → mitral/tufted cells (olfactory bulb) → lateral olfactory stria → **pyriform cortex/uncus, amygdala, entorhinal cortex** (area 28/34). Olfactory receptor neurons regenerate.

**Hippocampus (subiculum) → fornix → mammillary bodies → mammillothalamic tract → anterior thalamic nucleus → cingulate gyrus → (cingulum) → entorhinal cortex → hippocampus.**
Mnemonic for the main relays: "Some Merry Mothers Are Extremely Silly".

Output via **alveus → fimbria → crus → body → columns of the fornix** → mostly postcommissural to the **mammillary bodies**. Entorhinal cortex → perforant path → dentate gyrus → CA3 → CA1 → subiculum.
Function: consolidation of **recent** memory (not remote). Bilateral hippocampal loss → anterograde amnesia; unilateral fornix injury usually tolerated.
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 56–57. CA1 (Sommer sector) is most vulnerable to hypoxia.

cards.rueckseite: In the **substantia innominata** (basal forebrain, below the globus pallidus). Main source of **cortical acetylcholine**; degenerates in **Alzheimer disease**.

zeilen: Spinocerebellar tracts → fastigial, interposed nuclei; tone, gait, limb coordination
Pontine nuclei → dentate → VL thalamus; planning, fine coordination

cards.rueckseite:
3 layers: **molecular** (basket, stellate: inhibitory), **Purkinje** (GABA, the **only output** of the cortex, inhibitory to deep nuclei), **granular** (granule cells = only **excitatory** intrinsic cells, glutamate; Golgi cells inhibitory).
Inputs: **climbing fibers** (only from the **inferior olive**, 1:1 on Purkinje cells) and **mossy fibers** (all other sources, via granule cells/parallel fibers).

zeilen: Afferent: olivocerebellar, dorsal spinocerebellar, cuneocerebellar, vestibular; efferent: fastigial → vestibular nuclei
Purely afferent: pontocerebellar (from contralateral cortex via pons)
Main efferent: dentate/interposed → contralateral red nucleus and VL thalamus; afferent: ventral spinocerebellar

cards.rueckseite:
**Dorsal:** from **Clarke column** (C8–L2), **uncrossed**, ipsilateral leg/lower trunk proprioception → **inferior** cerebellar peduncle. Arm equivalent: cuneocerebellar tract (accessory cuneate nucleus).
**Ventral:** crosses in the cord, enters via the **superior** peduncle, recrosses in the cerebellum (net ipsilateral). Arm equivalent: rostral spinocerebellar tract.

"**Don't Eat Greasy Food**": **Dentate** (largest; coordination, → VL thalamus), **Emboliform** + **Globose** (= interposed; tone/limb → red nucleus), **Fastigial** (midline; → vestibular nuclei, reticular formation; posture).
Deep nuclei are **excitatory**; olivary inputs are crossed.

Deficits are **ipsilateral** (double crossing) and improve with time.
**Hemisphere:** limb ataxia, dysmetria, intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, hypotonia, rebound, decomposition of movement.
**Vermis (anterior):** truncal/gait ataxia (e.g. alcoholic degeneration).
**Flocculonodular:** imbalance, nystagmus (e.g. medulloblastoma in children).
Worst deficits: lesions of the **dentate nucleus / superior cerebellar peduncle**.
